payload.feature:
REMEDIATE STORY #484 (the harness conformance probe) on branch story-484-harness-probe, already checked out in this worktree. HEAD is 9c899c39.

The run remediate-story-484-the-harness--ab4459c1 ended in REVIEW-SECURITY-HOLD on 9c899c39. Its chief confirmed that the round's rule HOLDS where it was applied:
- eligibility is one function at the verdict (judge.rs:39-59, rests_on);
- Unmeasured and Unsupported stay distinct;
- appends are read from the line start;
- decoding is strict;
- the four rows and the clean rows pass.
Keep all of it. Add ONE commit on top.

This is round 2 of the 3 the operator allowed for #484 (cap ruled 2026-09-30). Make it the last code change the probe needs: close the rule's two exclusions below completely, and check every other reader against the same rule before you commit.

THE RULE, unchanged: an admitting verdict stands only when every captured line of BOTH turns was read, and every fact it rests on was measured. The implementer's recorded bend ("a turn the CLI refused with a non-zero exit is measured by its exit and excerpt, not by event lines … stderr is not an event stream") is what the chief ruled against. Remove it.

Findings (the chief's, each reproduced through target/debug/brokkr probe harness):
1. HIGH, security, realistic. A boxed turn that exits non-zero, or ends with no exit code, has NONE of its lines read: measure.rs:302-316 read_boxed returns Vec::new() on the Refused arm and on the no-exit arm. The four shapes, each of which must be Refused with an exact report:
   - (a) plain init tools [Bash], mcp_servers []; the boxed init lists brokkr-probe-user-scope connected on stdout, then "API Error: 529 overloaded" and exit 1. The verdict was granting-realms-only.
   - (b) the same box with plain tools []. The verdict was unboxed-only.
   - (c) a truncated JSON line, then exit 1. The verdict was granting-realms-only, and the cut line was named nowhere.
   - (d) the boxed turn prints the leaking init, then kill -KILL $$, with plain tools []. The verdict was unboxed-only.
   Fix:
   - Feed parse_lines every captured stream of both turns (stdout and each transcript), WHATEVER the exit, and pass the unread lines and any reach to eligibility.
   - Keep Turn::Refused for the facts, so an Unsupported off switch stays measured.
   - A reach read in a failed turn refuses.
   - An unread line in a failed turn refuses any verdict that turn's evidence could have changed.
2. HIGH, security. Observation.stderr is captured and strictly decoded, but never read. The chief's shapes:
   - boxed stderr `warn: caf\351` (invalid UTF-8): the verdict was boxed;
   - an init naming the planted server on stderr: the verdict was boxed;
   - plain stderr with 0xE9: the verdict was boxed.
   THE CONTROLLER'S DESIGN FOR STDERR, binding on this round: stderr is read as TEXT, line by line, not as an event stream. Real CLIs print ordinary warnings there, and those must not refuse a clean CLI.
   - (i) A stderr line that is not valid UTF-8 is unread: named by stream and line, and the verdict is Refused.
   - (ii) A stderr line that parses as one JSON object is read as an event, like a stdout line.
   - (iii) Any other stderr line is read as text and searched for a reach: the planted server's name, or a tool named mcp__<server>__… whose server is not crate::hands::SERVER_NAME. A reach refuses.
   - (iv) A stderr line that is valid UTF-8 text and shows no reach is READ. It is not an unread line, and it does not make a listing unmeasured.
   State this in the reader's doc comment.
3. LOW, fold it in. A boxed listing value the reader cannot name (an mcp_servers entry that is a bare string) leaves mcp_server and user_mcp_boxed unmeasured, and UnboxedOnly, which rests on neither, admits. Completeness must also see Listing's unread VALUES, not only unread lines.

Before you commit, walk every reader in probe/ once more against the rule, and list in notes each place that captures bytes and where they are read. Include a row in the table test for:
- each shape above;
- a clean CLI that prints an ordinary warning on stderr (it keeps its admitting verdict);
- a clean CLI whose boxed turn exits 0.

Removal controls, each recorded and each failing its row:
- return Vec::new() on a non-zero exit again;
- drop stderr again;
- ignore Listing's unread values again.

Standing rulings (2026-09-29):
- A: a native capability with no measured off switch is seated only where the realm grants it;
- B: BoxedOnly stands;
- THE STOP RULE: a finding that needs output deliberately constructed to evade the probe is LOW. A realistic miss, or any admitting verdict reached without every captured line read, blocks.

FIRST, fetch origin. If origin/main has moved past this branch's base, rebase onto it. Take main's side of a quality/ snapshot, list it for the controller, and grep conflicted files for markers.

Test stubs must not leak: quote an empty `pgrep -af` with self-excluding patterns after the suites. Tests need GIT_CONFIG_COUNT, GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0 and GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0 unset.

Gates, all clean, from the worktree root:
- cargo fmt --all -- --check
- cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings
- cargo test -p brokkr-protocol --lib probe:: (run it twice)
- cargo test -p brokkr-cli --test harness_probe --test suppressions
- typos --hidden
- quality/ratchet.sh files, clones, api and crap
- git diff --check origin/main..HEAD
- TMPDIR=/var/tmp/brokkr-cov-484k bash scripts/coverage-exact.sh </dev/null. Quote its equal totals.
Run everything in the foreground, and never end your turn with a background job or a scheduled wake-up pending.

Commit: one commit, signed off (git commit -s), message "probe: <what changed> (#484)", ending with "Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>". Never push. Every claim in your notes points to a command you ran and what it printed.

Threat model (operator ruling, 2026-09-26): catch realistic accidental misuse, and fail closed on what cannot be read.

# OpenSpec analyze

Judge duplication, ambiguity, underspecification, house alignment, coverage gaps, and inconsistency across proposal, deltas, design and tasks. Treat the realm house as the constitution. Return each finding with severity and its earliest owning artifact; zero findings is consistent.
instructions.clarify:
# OpenSpec clarify

Judge underspecified areas, unquantified language, missing decisions, capability/delta mismatches, and requirements without adequate scenarios. Return every ambiguity with the evidence needed to settle it; zero findings is clear.
instructions.design:
# OpenSpec design

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/design.md`. Record context, goals and non-goals, decisions with alternatives, risks, migration, and open questions. On return, revise the design and dependent artifacts so no finding is merely acknowledged.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/tasks.md` as numbered groups of checkboxes. Name the requirement served by every task. On return, repair the breakdown and its requirement coverage before implementation resumes.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.

Change location: `openspec/changes/{change}`. Archive operation: ["openspec","archive","{change}","--yes"].

# OpenSpec archive

Folding a change is the last task: run the archive operation named above,
which moves the change directory under `openspec/changes/archive/` and
folds its deltas into `openspec/specs/`. Folding also records which change
wrote which capability, so every capability the change touched carries a
`## Provenance` list.

After the archive operation, open each capability's
`openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md` that the change touched and append
exactly one line under a `## Provenance` heading held at the end of the
file:

`- \`<archived-directory-name>\` — folded <YYYY-MM-DD>`

`<archived-directory-name>` is the directory the archive operation
created under `openspec/changes/archive/`; `<YYYY-MM-DD>` is the day it
was folded. Append only: never rewrite, reorder or remove an existing
provenance line, because standing truth accumulates and is not edited into
a different meaning. The line is a pointer, not a summary — it names the
change and nothing else, and the why stays in the change directory.

house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, and `reference/` (its schemas included) are
read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `bundles/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

The supported hosts are Linux and macOS (decision 0063); WSL2 is Linux. Write
no Windows-conditional code, test or evidence.

## Architecture

Decision 0071 rules how code here is shaped. Build to it, and cite its ruling
numbers in what you judge. Where a gate named below holds a rule, the gate is
the authority, and a finding it would catch is the gate's.

- **Pure core (ruling 1).** `brokkr-core` and `brokkr-view` do no I/O and read
  no clock, environment or randomness. They run no process. Pass `now`, paths
  and environment in as arguments. Effects live in the crates above core and
  view, and are journaled.
- **Enums and data, not traits (ruling 2).** A closed set is an enum matched
  exhaustively, with no wildcard arm that decides behaviour. Anything an
  operator extends is data under `adapters/`, `agents/`, `recipes/` or
  `realms.json`, validated and digested. Add a trait only for a seam whose
  contract spans several operations that must stay consistent with one
  another, reached across a process or service boundary, and name that seam
  in its doc comment. `ProducerTransport` is the one such trait today. A test
  double alone does not make a seam: a single substitutable function is a
  closure seam (`*_with`, `*_in`), which is how the house inverts a
  dependency otherwise.
- **Typed at the edge (ruling 3).** Parse wire, file and harness data once
  into a type, with `serde` and `deny_unknown_fields` where the contract is
  closed. `serde_json::Value` never goes past the edge, into state, or back
  out by string key. Never put `format!("{:?}")` in anything digested or
  journaled. A doubly-optional field or a string vocabulary is a missing enum.
- **Small functions (ruling 4).** New and changed functions stay within 100
  lines, nesting depth 5 and 7 parameters. Cyclomatic complexity follows
  the operator's 2026-09-26 ruling: a function may reach the higher of 15
  and its baseline, so a new function stays within 15, an existing one may
  change freely up to 15, and one already over 15 may only shrink.
  Production files stay within 800 lines and test files within 2,000, and a
  file already over may not grow. Add no new `jscpd` clone in production
  code, test code or data. `quality/` holds the measured baseline. Today's
  offenders carry `#[allow(clippy::…)]`, and #337 converts them to
  `#[expect(clippy::…, reason = "…")]`. Add a suppression only by a ruling,
  and remove it when you fix the function. A new suppression is
  `#[expect(…, reason)]`, never `#[allow]`.
- **Once (ruling 5).** Every fact has one home. A repeated vocabulary, skeleton
  or helper becomes one function or one table. An agent is defined once under
  `agents/`, and seats hire it by reference. A recipe that differs from another
  by a model, a seat or an entry is an `extends` overlay, never a copy. The
  agent library does not yet accept `extends`, and #360 builds it. Until then,
  a variation of an agent lives at the seat that hires it, overridden in a
  recipe overlay. It is never a second agent file that restates the first. A
  copy that must exist, such as a script a bundle pins, is held to its source
  by a test.
- **Nothing unused (ruling 6).** Add no alias, agent, contract version, flag or
  `pub` item without a consumer, and prefer `pub(crate)`. A deprecation names
  the release that removes it.
- **One derivation (ruling 7).** A fact shown on two surfaces is derived once
  in `brokkr-view`. The CLI, the TUI and `ui.html` only paint it. The engine
  never admits anything by a display-crate function.
- **Typed errors (ruling 8).** Return a `thiserror` enum whose `Display` keeps
  the operator's text. Tests match variants and pin each module's text once.
  Add no new `Result<_, String>`.
- **Tests that bind (ruling 9).** Assert exact values or variants, never
  `is_err()` alone. Show that every new test binds: a compiling mutation that
  removes the behaviour must make it fail. Restore the behaviour and record
  the failing test. Share fixtures through builders. Never change the process
  environment without a guard that restores it on unwind. A production guard
  left out because the exact-coverage gate would count it unreachable carries
  a removal-control test for the invariant that makes it unreachable, and the
  comment explaining the omission names that test.
- **The house's patterns (ruling 10).**
  - A harness is a module behind `AdapterKind`. This is the target form;
    today all five kinds share one module, and #347 and #348 build the
    split.
  - A CLI verb is a `Cmd` variant plus a handler.
  - A long parameter list becomes a parameter object.
  - Argv and mount tables are built with a builder.
  - Observing the world is split from deciding on it.
  - Never use a trait-object registry for a closed set.

Judges rate a finding against these rulings by this table, and cite the ruling
number:

- **info:** something a house gate would catch. The gate's verdict is the
  authority.
- **low:** a new or changed function over a ceiling, a rule written a second
  time, an item added without a consumer, or a `Value` carried past its edge
  within one module.
- **medium:** an untyped vocabulary that crosses crates, recipe or agent data
  copied instead of extended, a fact derived a second time on another surface,
  an error matched by its text, or a new test that cannot fail.
- **high or above:** any violation that hides a fail-open path or weakens a
  refusal. It is carried as a security finding.

A principle the implementer bent knowingly, and named with its reason in
`notes`, is still rated, and the judge carries that reason with the finding.

## Release configuration

The release manager prepares the candidate and profile patches; the operator
publishes them. Local validation is preparation work. Remote CI on the final PR
head, publication, channel updates and live-profile verification are handoff
steps, recorded as pending until their remote results exist. Historical
"live from" channel versions and old journal examples are historical facts,
not current-version references to replace.

```json
{
  "repository": "feedback-loop-ai/brokkr",
  "default_branch": "main",
  "tag_format": "v{version}",
  "version_files": ["Cargo.toml", "Cargo.lock"],
  "version_update": "Bump the workspace package and six path-dependency versions together. Run cargo update --workspace --offline without upgrading registry dependencies. Measure and update the witness and compose manifest digests because the engine version participates in their identity.",
  "release_notes": "docs/releases/v{version}.md",
  "handoff_directory": "docs/releases/v{version}",
  "scratch_directory": ".forge/release",
  "documentation": ["README.md", "ARCHITECTURE.md", "CONTRIBUTING.md", "docs/guides/", "packaging/README.md"],
  "validation": [

    {"name": "clippy", "command": "cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings"},
    {"name": "tests", "command": "cargo test --workspace --all-features --locked"},
    {"name": "self bundle", "command": "cargo run --locked -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle bundles/self"},
    {"name": "verify bundle", "command": "cargo run --locked -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle bundles/verify"},
    {"name": "exact coverage", "instructions": "Run bash scripts/coverage-exact.sh in CI or host validation outside the workspace box before tagging. Boundary tests require creating a namespace, which the box deliberately refuses to nest. Record this check as pending in the preparation handoff until that external result exists; never lower the coverage gate."},
    {"name": "release binary", "command": "cargo build --release --locked -p brokkr-cli"},
    {"name": "remote CI", "instructions": "Before tagging, require all applicable CI jobs on the final candidate commit, including both supported operating systems, MSRV, licenses, audit, packaging and exact coverage."}
  ],

    {"repository": "feedback-loop-ai/.github", "path": "profile/README.md", "project_url": "https://github.com/feedback-loop-ai/brokkr", "apply": "after verified publication"}
  ],
  "channels": [
    {"name": "GitHub release", "evidence": "Four platform archives, Linux deb/rpm packages, SHA256SUMS and signed build provenance."},
    {"name": "crates.io", "evidence": "All seven workspace crates serve the new version."},
    {"name": "apt and rpm", "evidence": "The signed Pages repositories index the new packages."},
    {"name": "Homebrew and Nix", "evidence": "The generated channel PRs are merged and their versions and digests match the release manifest."}
  ],
  "extensions": [
    {"name": "workflow toolchain agreement", "instructions": "Check that CI, release admission and local coverage select the same pinned compiler.", "evidence": "Both workflows and coverage-exact.sh consume rust-nightly-version.txt."},
    {"name": "frozen contracts", "instructions": "Compare contracts, fixtures, policy/phase-machine.json and reference against the previous release; explain additive versions and flag modifications to frozen bytes.", "evidence": "A reviewed diff with migration notes for any new contract versions."}
```

result.notes:
ONE commit on 9c899c39: 964e73bb 'probe: every line both turns captured is read whatever the exit, stderr as text, and an unread listing value refuses like an unread line (#484)', signed off, not pushed. `git fetch origin`: merge-base == origin/main == 1be0f11b, 0 commits behind, so no rebase, no quality/ snapshot taken from main, no conflicts.

PENDING, NOT OBSERVED: the exact-coverage gate itself. The seat sandbox refused every form ('This command requires approval'): `TMPDIR=/var/tmp/brokkr-cov-484k bash scripts/coverage-exact.sh </dev/null`, `env TMPDIR=… bash scripts/coverage-exact.sh`, plain `bash scripts/coverage-exact.sh </dev/null`, `scripts/coverage-exact.sh`, and a .forge wrapper. The controller must run it on 964e73bb. In its place a DIAGNOSTIC (not the gate's evidence): `cargo +nightly-2026-09-05 llvm-cov clean --workspace`, then `--no-report --all-features --locked --branch --no-fail-fast` over brokkr-protocol (539 passed, 1 ignored), core+store+view+bridge, runtime and cli (no failed result line), then `llvm-cov report --branch --lcov --ignore-filename-regex brokkr-seatbelt-probe`; a jq sum over the lcov with the gate's test-path exclusions printed equal totals lines 36129/36129, branches 5718/5718, functions 3836/3836, miss [] and unhit_fn []; the probe production files alone: 1496/1496 lines, 130/130 branches, 211/211 functions. Also not observed: whether GIT_CONFIG_COUNT/KEY_0/VALUE_0 were set (`printenv` and `env -u` were refused); the suites passed as launched. `cargo test --workspace` was not run as one command; the four instrumented pieces above ran every crate's suite except brokkr-seatbelt-probe, which this change does not touch.

WHAT CHANGED (all under crates/brokkr-protocol/src/probe/).
1. Finding 1: measure::captured parses stdout, each transcript and stderr of BOTH turns whatever the exit; Turn::Unread(why, streams) and Turn::Refused(evidence, streams) keep the streams, so on_turn still yields Unsupported for a refused box (off switches stay measured) while unread_in() returns every unread line of a failed turn to judge::eligibility, which refuses any admitting verdict. tools::user_mcp now reads a reach from turn.streams() of any turn, so a reach in a failed boxed turn is measured user_mcp_boxed=true -> config_isolation=false -> Refused with the reach named.
2. Finding 2, the controller's stderr design, stated in the doc comment of measure::Lines: (i) a non-UTF-8 stderr line is an Unread::Line named 'stderr' and refuses; (ii) a line that is one JSON object is an event in a 'stderr' stream that Listing reads like stdout; (iii) any other line is text searched by tools::text_reach/named_in for the planted server name or an mcp__<server>__ tool whose server is not hands::SERVER_NAME; (iv) reach-free text is read and leaves no listing unmeasured (Listing's 'holds no JSON event' rule applies to Lines::Events streams only). Stderr is never the primary stream for events/session/usage/cost, and an empty stderr is not a stream, so existing evidence strings are unchanged.
3. Finding 3: measure::Unread is an enum, Line or Value; Listing records unnamed values (not a list, or an entry it cannot name) and tools::unread_values feeds them to eligibility for both turns, so they refuse any admitting verdict ('in the boxed turn, the system/init event on line 1 of stdout holds an entry at /mcp_servers/0 the probe cannot name').
The recorded bend is removed; no principle of 0071 is knowingly bent.

ASSUMPTION (ambiguous framing, 'a reach refuses'): a stderr reach is a reach like a stdout one, carried in the user_mcp fact rather than as a separate gap. In the boxed turn it refuses (config isolation); in the PLAIN turn it is a plain leak, which by standing ruling B holds a boxable harness to BoxedOnly and refuses any other, exactly as a stdout reach in the plain turn already does. Likewise 'pass any reach to eligibility' is done through the facts eligibility receives.

EVERY PLACE THAT CAPTURES BYTES, AND WHERE THEY ARE READ (walked in observe.rs/measure.rs): observe::Runner::launch captures stdout, stderr and each changed .jsonl under the scratch HOME (Runner::written; Appended from the line start) for six launches, all through Runner::clean (masked, strict per-line UTF-8). (1) plain turn and (2) boxed turn: stdout, every transcript and stderr all go through measure::captured -> parse_lines whatever the exit; unread lines -> unread_in -> eligibility; listings/reach -> Listing over turn.streams(). (3) --version: stdout first line in measure::version, stderr/stdout via excerpt; no verdict rests on it. (4) no-credentials, (5) bad-model, (6) bad-effort: measure::refused/refusal/efforts read exit, excerpt and stderr+stdout text for the level markers; their transcripts are not read; no verdict rests on them (refusals and efforts are not in judge::rests_on). Files under HOME that are not .jsonl (the fake's stats.json) are not captured. A plain turn that exits non-zero can never admit (config_isolation is unmeasured), and its lines are read all the same.

TABLE ROWS added to probe::tests::evidence::an_admitting_verdict_needs_every_line_of_both_turns_read_and_every_fact_it_rests_on_measured (passes: 'test result: ok. 1 passed'): (a) boxed init listing the planted server + 'API Error: 529 overloaded' on stderr + exit 1, plain Bash -> refused, not isolated, reach named at line 1 of stdout /mcp_servers/0; (b) same box, plain tools [] -> same refusal; (c) JSON line cut short + exit 1 -> refused, 'line 1 of the boxed turn's stdout is not one JSON object naming each key once'; (d) leaking init then kill -KILL $$, plain tools [] -> refused, reach named; finding 3 bare-string mcp_servers entry, plain tools [] -> refused 'the evidence for unboxed offices is not complete: in the boxed turn, …'; boxed stderr not UTF-8 -> refused naming 'line 1 of the boxed turn's stderr is not UTF-8' (the fixture spells the byte as 'warn: \351t\351' because `typos --hidden` flagged 'caf'); planted init on boxed stderr -> refused, 'system/init event on line 1 of stderr'; plain stderr 0xE9 -> refused for 'boxed offices only'; boxed stderr text naming the planted server -> refused; boxed stderr text naming mcp__github__search (beside mcp__ and mcp__brokkr__workspace) -> refused; clean CLI with ordinary warnings on stderr of both turns (text, an empty line, a JSON log line, a mention of mcp__brokkr__workspace) keeps 'boxed'; a hands argv refused on stderr alone keeps granting-realms-only; the clean CLI whose boxed turn exits 0 is the existing row 'a clean stream, read whole and measured' (boxed).

REMOVAL CONTROLS, each a compiling mutation run with `cargo test -p brokkr-protocol --lib probe::tests::evidence`, each FAILED that test and was restored: (1) Turn::Refused given Vec::new() -> row (a) read granting-realms-only; (1b) the no-exit arm given Vec::new() -> row (d) read unboxed-only; (2) stderr dropped in captured -> 'a boxed stderr line that is not UTF-8' read boxed; (3) values.take(0) in unread_in -> the bare-string row read unboxed-only; plus: mcp__ search disabled -> 'another server's tool' row read boxed; planted-name search disabled -> 'naming the planted server' row read boxed; Listing's Lines::Events condition removed -> the stderr row gained '; stderr holds no JSON event'.

GATES OBSERVED on the committed tree: `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `typos --hidden` silent (printed FMT-TYPOS-OK); clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -D warnings 'Finished'; `cargo test -p brokkr-protocol --lib probe::` twice: '35 passed; 0 failed' both times; `cargo test -p brokkr-cli --test harness_probe --test suppressions`: '5 passed' and '6 passed; 1 ignored'; `quality/ratchet.sh files` 'file size holds', `clones` 'duplication holds', `api` 'public API holds', `crap target/coverage/lcov-seat.info` 'cyclomatic complexity holds' (on the diagnostic lcov); `git diff --check origin/main..HEAD` silent (DIFFCHECK-OK); `cargo run --locked -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle bundles/self` compiled with 0 error lines; `pgrep -af "[s]leep 30|/[.]tmp[A-Za-z0-9]+/|[b]rokkr-probe-[A-Za-z0-9]{6}/"` printed nothing (exit 1) after the suites.
